subject: Reservation failover window & queueing behavior — amendment request (Sentinel AI)
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha@sentinel.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool failover / queueing behavior — request for amendment

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — performance looks promising. Before we finalize the reserved GPU contract, a couple of operational items popped up from our infra and contracts teams that I wanted to put on your radar:

1) Failover window: we saw a couple brief preemptions on your demo pool last month and want explicit language on the expected failover/drain window for reserved pools. Our product team needs an upper bound (seconds) for cold-fallback / model-switching behavior to plan client-side timeouts.

2) Queueing/priority semantics: when a reserved pool is partially drained and requests enter fallback routing, how do you prioritize reserved vs best-effort requests? We need guarantees for tail latency under the reserved commitment.

3) Credits/recourse: if we experience repeated failover events beyond the agreed window, Contracts wants a simple crediting mechanism instead of manual escalation.

Can you share proposed SLA language or a short addendum we can review? Happy to take a quick call if it speeds things up.

Best,
Asha
Director, Platform Ops
Sentinel AI

P.S. cc'ing our contracts alias to loop them in for any legal/credit language: contracts@sentinel.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Asha Reddy <asha@sentinel.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool failover / queueing behavior — technical proposal

Naomi / Diego / Asha — quick technical summary and proposal from infra: 

- Failover/drain window: For a reserved pool with active KV cache, the typical failover path (detect node loss, re-route to backup replica, warm KV region) completes in 30–90s depending on model size. To be conservative, we propose a 60s nominal upper bound for single-node preemptions in a multi-node reserved pool (99th percentile).

- Queueing semantics: During partial capacity loss we apply a two-tier admission policy:
  * Reserved capacity requests are admitted preferentially into the reserved pool queue until per-tenant concurrency is exhausted.
  * Excess reserved requests are routed to a logically compatible fallback model (same family, lower quantization) with a signal header so customers can choose to retry or accept fallback.

- Tail latency: We can guarantee a tail token-latency SLA for requests served from the reserved pool (when capacity is intact). For requests that are routed to fallback we provide an SLA for routing time (we recommend 500ms median router latency, but cannot guarantee generation tail for fallback variants).

- Credits: suggest automatic credit of 5% of monthly reserved fees per incident where the failover window exceeds the agreed bound by >30s, capped at 25% per quarter. (Diego — please sanity-check the commercial/legal side.)

I can draft a short addendum that captures these points. Asha — does 60s sound workable for you? If you need stricter numeric limits we can discuss options (e.g., higher reservation granularity or pinned high-availability pools at higher price).

-Karthik
Principal, Inference Infrastructure

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Reddy <asha@sentinel.ai>, Sentinel AI Contracts <contracts@sentinel.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool failover / queueing behavior — draft SLA language attached

Adding commercial/legal framing and attaching a draft addendum. Key points in the draft (attached PDF):

- Definition: "Failover Window" = elapsed time from first node degradation detection to routing completion to alternate capacity for affected requests. Excludes scheduled maintenance windows with >=72h notice.

- Commitment: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to keep Failover Window <= 60 seconds for multi-node reserved pools, measured at 99th percentile on a monthly basis.

- Priority/Queueing: Reserved requests get admission priority and bounded per-tenant concurrency; in cases where instant capacity is unavailable Redwood will route to a fallback model variant and annotate responses with X-Redwood-Fallback: true.

- Remedy: For any calendar month where measured monthly 99th percentile Failover Window for Sentinel's reserved pool exceeds 60s by more than 30s, Redwood will credit Sentinel 5% of that month's reserved pool fee per incident, up to 25% of total monthly fees.

- Canary and monitoring: We propose daily synthetic checks and a 30-day canary period post-go-live; Sentinel will get 30-day rolling performance dashboards in the Console.

Attachments:
- redwood-sla-amendment-draft-20260622.pdf (SLA addendum with trackable sections)
- sentinel_queue_profile.csv (sample concurrency and burst profile sent by Sentinel)

Naomi — feel free to send this to Asha with the attachments. Asha — Diego and I can join a short call if Contracts has redlines.

—Diego
Senior Product Manager, Runtime Reliability

- Priority: Reserved requests prioritized; fallback routing to compatible model variants with X-Redwood-Fallback headers.
- Credits: 5% monthly reserved fee per qualifying incident (exceeding 60s by >30s), capped at 25% per quarter.
- Monitoring: Shared daily synthetics and 30-day post-go-live canary.

Naomi / team —

Thanks for the quick draft. We reviewed and attached a redline with a few asks:

1) Measurement: please clarify sampling methodology for the 99th percentile — we request a clause that allows a shared sampling export for audit (rolling 90 days).
2) Credits: instead of per-incident credits, Contracts proposes an aggregate monthly shortfall calculation to avoid fragmentation of many small incidents.
3) Fallback routing: please add an opt-out for routing to fallback variants for a short list of routes we control; we can elect to queue client-side for up to 3 minutes in specific latency-tolerant paths.

Attached: sentinel-redline-20260623.pdf
